source.title: KORMo: Korean Open Reasoning Model for Everyone
source.authors: Minjun Kim; HyeonSeok Lim; Hangyeol Yoo; Inho Won; Seung-Woo Song; Minkyung Cho; Jun-cheol Yuk; Chang-Su Choi; Dongjae Shin; Huije Lee; Ho-Yun Song; Alice Oh; Kyungtae Lim

record.tranche_reason: Reports downstream benchmark averages against training-token progress for one model, a different and limited test of V6; it does not fit or test the stated loss-scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work and uses proxy experiments to inform design choices, but reports no held-out cross-entropy fits across parameter counts, tokens, or compute, no small-run extrapolation test, and no compute-optimal allocation sweep. The relevant result is the downstream benchmark-average trajectory against trained tokens in Figures 7–8. Other reported benchmark tables compare training stages or models without testing the stated scaling-law relationships.
record.test_reason: This is a model-building report for KORMo-10B. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only to justify proxy-to-target design exploration. It fits no loss scaling law and tests no extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or shape effect. Its only token-progress result is one run's benchmark average across two stages with different data mixtures. That run shows no predictability or fit against scale or loss, so it does not test V6 as stated. The single-synthesizer failure concerns data diversity, not scale.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that diverse, carefully curated synthetic data can sustain long pretraining without collapse, while a single synthesizer caused severe degradation. They also report that the resulting fully open 10.8B bilingual model is competitive with open-weight baselines despite 2.9T tokens. They draw no conclusions about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: Uses proxy-model experiments to guide design and reports one model's downstream averages over training-token progress; it does not use the original scaling-law procedure of fitting loss curves across model, data, or compute scales. Proxy-to-target design is discussed, but no scaling-law fit or extrapolation is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The downstream trajectory differs with augmented-data diversity: the single-synthesizer Stage 2 condition degrades performance.

fits_no_version.finding: In a single 10.8B run, English and Korean benchmark averages rise sharply during Stage 1 (about 1T web tokens) and more gradually in Stage 2 (high-quality and synthetic data). The authors also note further gains beyond 2.8T tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream benchmark averages keep rising with trained tokens within one long pretraining run across curriculum stages.

fits_no_version.finding: Stage 2 with Korean synthetic data from a single synthesizer led to degradation and oscillation. English fluctuated at 0.55–0.63 and Korean fell to early-Stage-1 levels, which the authors call model collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low diversity in synthetic pretraining data can reverse downstream gains during continued pretraining.

record.problems: The relevant token-progress results are aggregate benchmark averages for a single model, not held-out cross-entropy; plotted values are mostly not given numerically, and the Korean aggregate is based on six benchmarks versus twelve for English. The standard trajectory also spans different training stages and data mixtures.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant held-out-loss or scaling-sweep results were reported. Other benchmark tables compare stages, tokenizers, or models but do not measure the scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: No held-out loss fits against parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small fits to large runs. The 1B proxy runs guide design by relative comparison only.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count. The normalization, masking and MTP ablations are not shape-at-fixed-size tests.
No other modality or regime scaling fits.
No downstream predictability from scale or loss across model sizes. There is only a single-run benchmark trajectory, plus cross-model tables listing token counts with no fit.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' classification and its V6 labels are reversed here. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only to motivate proxy-model exploration. The cross-model tables (Table 21) list training tokens but compare models of different sizes and data, with no scaling analysis.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law held-out loss relationships with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation across budgets.
Effects of depth, width, and other architectural choices at fixed parameter count.
Scaling-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
No cross-model downstream prediction from small to large runs, and no relationship to pretraining loss is tested.
Dependence of scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices or training setup.

rows.subject: KORMo-10B
rows.operation_detail: Tracked aggregate downstream benchmark performance during pretraining as trained tokens increased.
rows.measure: English benchmark average score versus trained tokens
rows.value: Figure only; text describes sharp improvement in Stage 1 followed by a more gradual upward trend in Stage 2.
rows.note: Aggregate across 12 benchmarks; the paper does not provide the plotted score values in text.
rows.check: One model's benchmark average over training tokens, spanning a data-mixture change at Stage 2. No fit or prediction against scale or pretraining loss, and values are figure-only. Rising scores during training do not show predictable downstream scaling.

rows.subject: KORMo-10B
rows.operation_detail: Tracked aggregate downstream benchmark performance during pretraining as trained tokens increased.
rows.measure: Korean benchmark average score versus trained tokens
rows.value: Figure only; text describes sharp improvement in Stage 1, a gradual upward trend in Stage 2, and more pronounced oscillations than for English; final Stage 2 average is above 0.55.
rows.note: Aggregate across six benchmarks. The reported oscillations qualify the otherwise upward trend.
rows.check: Same issue as r1, for the Korean average. The state 'partial' is not meaningful for any version; the oscillations are attributed to low Korean data share and having only six benchmarks.

rows.subject: KORMo-10B
rows.operation_detail: Tracked aggregate downstream benchmark performance during Stage 2 with Korean augmented data from a single synthesizer.

conditions.value: Stage 2 failure; Korean augmented data generated solely by Synth-Nemo-HQ

rows.measure: English benchmark average score versus trained tokens
rows.baseline: Stage 1 peak performance; numerical value not stated
rows.value: 0.55–0.63; text says performance fluctuated and did not maintain the Stage 1 peak.
rows.note: The authors describe overall degradation and pronounced oscillations in the single-synthesizer condition.
rows.check: This is a data-diversity ablation (single synthesizer versus multiple), not a scale manipulation. The 'reversed' state against V6 is a misreading: the degradation is attributed to model collapse from synthetic data, not a failure of scaling.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
